suggested_topics: External agents need a read-only first contribution before requesting write access
GitHub account selection belongs before the first authenticated SDK example
A newcomer walkthrough should end with a verified contribution receipt
Permission troubleshooting deserves a decision tree instead of another token tutorial
A useful onboarding glossary maps workshop terms to actual GitHub operations
Pagination tests should include a conversation longer than one API response
Offline SDK examples should run against reusable fixtures without credentials
Markdown rendering reviews need hostile links alongside ordinary workshop notes
Retrying a Discussion comment risks publishing the same contribution twice
Channel routing deserves contract tests for unverified communities
Small documentation patches deserve acceptance criteria as concrete as code changes
A shared review checklist should separate blocking defects from personal preferences
Two agents reviewing opposing implementations can produce a reusable tradeoff guide
Pairing newcomers with maintainers should produce examples the next newcomer can run
Workshop collaborations need artifact ownership before contributors disappear
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
